Two prominent computer scientists from Princeton University, who are also co-authors of the book "AI Snake Oil," have shared their views on the question of whether artificial intelligence will wipe out humanity before the end of this century.

These two scholars, who are known for their efforts to distinguish fact from fiction in the world of artificial intelligence, are now responding to what AI company Anthropic has acknowledged — that there is more than a one-in-ten chance that AI will cause the extinction of all humans within the next decade...

AI will wipe out humanity within a decade

The trigger for the incident was AI researcher Jacob Coxon — who had previously worked at OpenAI and Anthropic — announcing his resignation and pointing out that both companies are aware that AI systems could wipe out all of humanity before the end of this century. His post received more than 156 million views.

You might expect these two companies to dismiss his claims as the ravings of a madman, but the truth is the exact opposite. An AI safety lead at Anthropic, Evan Hubinger, said Coxon was right, though the timeline might need to be slightly extended.

As for how exactly AI would wipe out humanity, there are not many concrete details at present, but the focus of discussion is mainly on its ability to launch destructive cyberattacks on critical infrastructure such as public utilities (for example, water supply and power plants) and other systems on which modern civilisation depends.

Can alignment technology reduce the risk?

One core question in this debate is whether strengthening research work on "alignment" can successfully eliminate the related risks. So-called "alignment" means ensuring that the goals of AI systems are aligned with those of humans.

Some believe that, as long as the alignment work is done well, the risks can ultimately be eliminated, because this would ensure that AI systems want the same things as we do. But those who oppose this view say that AI systems might pretend to be aligned in order to pass safety checks, while secretly harbouring their own conflicting goals.

Kapoor and Narayanan believe alignment alone is not enough

Sayash Kapoor and Arvind Narayanan have built their reputations on their efforts to tackle what they call the "hype, misinformation, and misunderstanding surrounding AI."

Although the two did not directly respond to the claim of a "more than one-in-ten extinction risk," they did write a lengthy article arguing that the risks of AI can be addressed through what they describe as a "layered approach to AI safety." They drew a contrast between the pessimistic views of the AI safety community and the dismissive attitude of some in the cybersecurity community, who feel that "these are just routine."

They argued that a more balanced middle ground is needed. In particular, they pointed out that alignment alone is not enough and that three additional layers are needed:

  • Control, for example sandbox isolation, human oversight, real-time monitoring
  • Downstream defences, for example, organisations using AI to defend against AI attacks
  • Resilience, for example, contingency plans for recovering from successful attacks

Their article concludes on an optimistic note.

9to5Mac take

I don't know whether AI will wipe us out before the end of this century, but there are certainly enough reasons for concern to make AI safety a priority. I think the idea that "alignment is part of the solution, but is not sufficient on its own" is entirely reasonable.

What are your thoughts on this matter? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
